ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b$ passes through points $A(2,1)$ and $B(-1,-2)$. What is the solution set for the inequality $-2<kx+b<1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Because the line $y=kx+b$ passes through points $A(2, 1)$ and $B(-1, -2)$, \\
therefore $\begin{cases}2k+b=1\\ -k+b=-2\end{cases}$, solving this yields $\begin{cases}k=1\\ b=-1\end{cases}$,\\
Because $-2<kx+b<1$,\\
therefore $-2<x-1<1$,\\
therefore $\begin{cases}x-1<1\\ x-1>-2\end{cases}$, solving this gives $-1<x<2$,\\
hence, the answer is $x \in \boxed{(-1, 2)}$.
